Subject: Redwood hosted API pricing & comparison for FastShop

Hi Vanessa,

We're evaluating hosted LLM providers for FastShop's search & personalization layer and want a straightforward view of Redwood's baseline pricing and how you stack up against OpenAI, Anthropic, Together, and AWS (in particular the net effective pricing teams have quoted us). Procurement attached an RFQ with required terms and expected traffic profile.

Top asks:
- Baseline rate card for hosted generation and embeddings (token / unit pricing + any fixed per-request charges).
- Typical discounts for ASV / 12-month commitments.
- Any current marketplace or channel credits we could leverage.
- Notes on data handling (SOC 2 / data residency / DPA).
- If you're willing to match a competitor's net effective price (we can share redacted contract).

Estimated usage (from our side): ~300M tokens/month generation, ~2M embeddings/month, 95% US traffic, <150ms median generation latency target.

Thanks — procurement is cc'd. If you can send a short commercial summary we can circulate internally.

Best,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Product Partnerships
FastShop

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-29T10:02:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Redwood hosted API pricing & comparison for FastShop

Hi Elena — great to hear from you and thanks for the RFQ. I've pulled together a concise commercial summary below; I'm happy to set up a 30-minute call to walk through numbers.

Baseline hosted API (public catalog, US region):
- Text generation: $0.0018 / 1K tokens (base model family)
- Large-generation variant (higher throughput): $0.0026 / 1K tokens
- Embeddings: $0.0005 / embedding
- Streaming: no additional per-token surcharge (same token rate)
- Free trial credit and pilot: $10k credit for new enterprise pilots (one-time)
- Volume tiers: 10-100M tokens/month: 7% discount; 100-500M: 18% discount; 500M+: 28% discount (applied to base lists)

Commit discounts and commitments:
- 12-month commit: additional 8% off tiered price at 200M+ committed effective monthly volume
- Enterprise reserved capacity (Dedicated) available if you require isolation; pricing is separate (we can share a dedicated quote)

Security / compliance:
- SOC 2 Type II, DPA available, support for customer-managed keys (KMS) for Private deployments. Data residency options in us-east/us-west/eu-west.

Matching competitor pricing:
- We can discuss net-effective matching depending on contract terms and minimum commitment (we typically require a redacted competitor offer and a defined committed volume to consider a match).

Next steps:
- If you can confirm a 90-day pilot volume profile (approx tokens per day) and whether embeddings are served synchronously, I can put together a formal 1-page commercial proposal.

Attach: redwood_ratecard_v1.pdf

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa—

Thanks for the flag. Strategy recs below:

1) Commercial structure to offer:
- 12-month committed ARR with a 3-month ramp pilot. Commit at 250M tokens/month ASV.
- Offer a blended effective target: start with a 15% off list for Q1 (pilot + ramp), then a tiered rebate that targets a net effective $0.0013/1K at 250M sustained. If FastShop shares their competitor redacted pricing we can consider a one-time True-Up credit for the first quarter to match net-effective price (requires finance sign-off).

2) Concessions we can make without exec escalation:
- 15% off list across the first quarter + $10k pilot credit (already in ratecard).
- Commitment discount structure (no signature-level escalation if net price stays >= $0.0010/1K).

3) Things to involve legal/security for DPA:
- Provide SOC 2 Type II report and a DPA with a retention schedule clause. For hosted we can offer 90-day default logs, option to opt into longer retention in Dedicated.

4) Commercial levers:
- Reserved capacity / Dedicated conversion credit after 6 months if they want isolation.
- Marketplace credits if they come via cloud partner (avoid counting against list discount).

Action: Vanessa—send the 1-page proposal with the 15% pilot concession and the conditional true-up clause (subject to redacted competitor evidence). Finance will review the true-up mechanics; I'll loop in legal for DPA language.

-Rishi

Hi Elena — thanks for sharing the usage expectation and procurement form. Per internal review, here is a short commercial proposal we can proceed on quickly if it aligns with FastShop's procurement windows.

Proposal highlights (summary):
- Pilot: 3-month pilot (reduced ramp) with $10k Redwood pilot credit applied to invoices. During pilot we apply 15% off standard list prices.
- Commit: 12-month commitment at 250M tokens/month average. Post-pilot pricing will be tiered; target net effective price: $0.0013 / 1K tokens at the 250M committed level (mechanics: 18% tier discount + 8% commit).
- True-up clause: If FastShop shares a redacted competitor net-effective offer, Redwood will consider a one-time true-up credit for Q1 to match net-effective price (finance approval required).
- Embeddings: $0.00045 / embedding at committed volumes (5% additional discount over list).
- Security: SOC 2 Type II available; DPA with log-retention clause (default 90 days for hosted). We can discuss Dedicated if you require customer-managed keys or longer retention.
